findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0229_intake_batches.sql:1173-1198 (the `failed` facet of clara.get_intake_batch), corroborated by packages/db/migrations/0051_extraction_recovery_door.sql:1-45 ("terminal document_processing_tasks rows are IMMUTABLE")
findings.what: The `failed` facet counts a member as failed if ANY `document_processing_tasks_visible` row for its document has a non-null `error_code` — not the CURRENT/latest one. Because the estate's own extraction-recovery design (0051's header) makes a terminally-failed task row immutable and routes a successful retry through a fresh attempt, a document that failed once under load and then succeeded still carries a stale failed task row forever. The result: a batch member that is fully admitted, has a committed operation receipt, and is rendered under the card's `settled` facet with an 'Open Work' link ALSO appears under the `failed` facet with a badge reading 'Extraction failed' / 'Upload failed' and the SAME working 'Open Work' link (apps/web/components/documents/intake-batch-card.tsx:92-100 `rowStateKey`, :343-393 row rendering; the SQL selects `work_id` into the failed-facet rows unconditionally at 0229:1183-1189). This directly contradicts the ticket's own headline ("truthful overlapping Work facets") and AC3 ("completed means business completion"): 'settled' and 'failed' are not compatible overlapping states the way 'admitted' and 'waiting' are (CONTEXT.md's own overlap example) — a Work cannot honestly be both business-complete and extraction-failed on the same card.
findings.evidence: The report's own AC2 evidence line is the smoking gun: docs/plan/active/refresh-wave-2026-09-18/reports/636-final.md states the World-leg re-run measured `facets {admitted 95, settled 95, waiting 4, unassigned 4, failed 35}` with `zero host flakes this run` (so persistent.length=95 exactly matches admitted/settled). packages/runtime/tests/intake-batch-e2e.mjs deliberately engineers exactly ONE extraction-style failure (`failer`, lines 292-299, 329, 344, and the assertion at :373 `pack.facets.failed.count >= 1`) alongside one awaiting_fact, one awaiting_capacity and two unfiled members (lines 328-346) — nothing in the fixture explains the other 34 counted as 'failed' while simultaneously counted as 'settled'. No DB battery cell or web unit test ever constructs a member that is both settled and failed: packages/db/tests/intake-batch.test.mjs's only failed-facet test (lines 412-431) drives failure exclusively through `clara.fail_document_intake` (the intake-failure_code half of the OR, never the document_processing_tasks half), and apps/web/components/documents/intake-batch-card.test.tsx's `ready()` fixture (used by every state/facet test including `p636.card.child_addresses` at line 219) gives each facet a DISTINCT member — the overlap scenario the real World run hit is untested anywhere. The final report's AC2/AC3 rows are marked 'done' with this exact facet output quoted as evidence, without reconciling or even naming the 35-vs-1 discrepancy (the report's only related note, 'Follow-ups worth filing' #5, blames CI log noise/concurrency limits but never connects it to the fact that ~34 already-posted members are mislabelled failed on the durable board).
findings.fix: Change the `failed` facet's document_processing_tasks clause to look at the MOST RECENT task per document (e.g. `distinct on (document_id) ... order by created_at desc`) and/or exclude a document that already has a work_id with a committed receipt, so a member that recovered via a later attempt is not permanently shown as failed. Add a DB battery cell and a card unit test that construct exactly this scenario (a task row with error_code set, followed by a later successful admission+receipt for the same document) and assert the member appears ONLY under `settled`, never under `failed`. Re-run the World leg and confirm `failed.count` tracks the number of members the test actually intended to fail.

findings.where: apps/web/components/work/work-detail.tsx:271-283 (batchOrigin state), :434-450 (renderPosted gate), :763-778 (the row itself inside PostedEntrySection); apps/web/lib/work/reads.ts:195-214 (entry derives from work.result?.entry_id)
findings.what: DECISIONS §0 D5 / brief-636.md §3 require 'ONE row on Work detail ("part of batch X")' with no further qualification, and AC5 is specifically about exposing 'per-file failure/recovery and stable links' — i.e. the reverse navigation matters most for a waiting, running or failed child, not only a posted one. As built, `batchOrigin` is fetched unconditionally but the row is rendered only inside `PostedEntrySection`, which itself is rendered only when `entry !== null` (`renderPosted`, work-detail.tsx:434-436), and `entry` is populated only once the Work has posted a journal entry (`work.result?.entry_id`, lib/work/reads.ts:195). A member that is queued, running, cancelled, refused, or waiting on a dependency — i.e. every case AC4/AC5's recovery language is actually about — shows NO batch link at all on its Work detail page. The feature is silently narrowed to the one case (already posted) where the reverse link is least needed.
findings.evidence: Confirmed by direct code read: work-detail.tsx renders `renderPosted` (which is the only place `batchOrigin` reaches the DOM) strictly guarded by `entry === null ? null : <PostedEntrySection ... batchOrigin={batchOrigin} .../>` (lines 434-450), and `PostedEntrySection` only prints the row when `batchOrigin !== null` (lines 763-778). `entry` traces to `work.result?.entry_id` (lib/work/reads.ts:195), which is set only for a Work that has actually posted. Zero test coverage exists for this row anywhere in the repo: `grep -rl "work-batch-origin|batchOrigin|WorkBatchOrigin" apps/web` (excluding build output) returns only the two source files (work-detail.tsx, lib/documents/intake-batch.ts) and messages/en.json — no *.test.tsx, no e2e spec. The final report's AC5 row (636-final.md) claims 'done' with evidence 'one `work-batch-origin` row on Work detail' and no caveat about the posted-only gate or the absence of any test proving the row renders.
findings.fix: Move the batch-origin row out of PostedEntrySection into a block that renders regardless of posting status (e.g. beside WorkFacts, which already renders unconditionally), or add a second render path for the non-posted case. Add a work-detail unit test that mounts a Work with `entry === null` and a non-null `batchOrigin` and asserts the row is visible, plus the existing posted case.
